info.title: notifi
info.summary: Push notifications to an iPhone, iPad or Mac from one HTTP request.
info.description:
notifi delivers a push notification to the device that created the send key you authenticate with. There is no account: install the app, copy the send key it makes on first launch, and post a title and a body to notifi.it. Notification content is encrypted with the device’s public key before it is stored, so neither notifi nor Apple can read your notifications.

Send keys are minted on the device by a request signed with a private key that never leaves it. There is no endpoint that creates one, so an agent has to ask a human to copy the key out of the app’s Keys tab.

When to use it: a build, backup or training run that finished or failed; a CI job or deploy that broke; a coding agent that is done or is blocked on a decision; a cron job or home server that noticed something. It is not a way to reach anyone who has not given you one of their own keys, and delivery is best-effort, so it should not be the only path for anything where a missed notification causes harm.

get.summary: Send a notification with query parameters
get.description: The same operation as POST /send, for a quick test from a browser or a shell. A key in a query string ends up in edge logs and shell history, so prefer POST with an Authorization header, and rotate any key you have sent this way.

post.description: Delivers a notification to the device that created the send key. Answers 202 once the server has accepted it, which is not a delivery receipt. Query parameters win over body fields when both are present. The key body field also authenticates; the security schemes above cannot describe a credential in the body, so it is listed only as a field of SendParams.

sendKey.description: The send key from the app’s Keys tab, as Authorization: Bearer nk_yourkey. Preferred: a header is not written to edge logs or shell history.

keyParameter.name: key
keyParameter.description: The send key as a parameter. It appears in edge logs, in shell history and in any proxy in between, which makes it the weaker option: use it only for a quick test, and rotate the key afterwards.

key.name: key
key.description: The send key, if it is not sent as a bearer token.

link.name: link
link.description: A link to a website or internal app.

image.name: image
image.description: https URL of a PNG, JPEG or GIF up to 5 MB.

occurred_at.name: occurred_at
occurred_at.description: When the event actually happened, as unix milliseconds.

key.description: The send key, if it is not sent as a bearer token. Required unless sent as a bearer token. The key picks the device the notification lands on.

title.description: The notification title. A longer title is delivered cropped, with a warning in the response.

message.description: The notification body, in Markdown. A longer body is delivered cropped, with a warning.

link.description: A link to a website or internal app. Opened when the notification is tapped. https always opens; another scheme — shortcuts://run-shortcut?name=Deploy, an app’s own deep link — opens only when the key’s Open any link switch is on in the app; off, the link is hidden.

image.description: https URL of a PNG, JPEG or GIF up to 5 MB. One that cannot be fetched is dropped, with a warning, and the notification still arrives.

occurred_at.description: When the event actually happened, as unix milliseconds. For a queued or retried send. Only changes the timestamp shown in the app; defaults to the time the server accepted the request.

is_critical.description: Breaks through Focus. The key must also have critical alerts switched on in the app, or an ordinary notification is delivered and the response carries a warnings array.

warnings.description: Present only when the notification was delivered differently from what was asked: a cropped title or body, a dropped image, or a critical alert delivered as an ordinary notification.

code.description: Read error.code, not code: the code is nested one level down.

message.description: A readable explanation, in the language negotiated from Accept-Language.

Accepted.description: The server accepted the notification. Not a delivery receipt.

warnings: Sent as a normal notification: critical alerts are switched off for this key.

UnexpectedError.description: Any other failure, in the same error shape: not_found or internal_error.

InvalidRequest.description: A parameter is missing or malformed.

UnknownKey.description: The key is unknown or has been revoked.

InvalidContent.description: The device is set to refuse a notification it cannot deliver as written.

error.message: Not sent. This device is set to refuse a notification it cannot deliver as written.

RateLimited.description: Over the hourly device limit or the per-minute IP limit. Carries a Retry-After header with the seconds until the window resets.

error.message: Too many notifications. Try again shortly.
